beats: Somewhere in Australia, an animal is pooping perfect little cubes!
It's the wombat, a chubby burrower with very short legs.
Every night, it leaves dozens of cubes on rocks and logs to mark its turf.
For years, nobody knew how a round tube could make a square poo.
Then a scientist in Australia sent two engineers in Atlanta the guts of two roadkill wombats, frozen!
One of them said they opened those intestines like it was Christmas!
They slid long skinny balloons inside and blew them up, to see where the gut stretched.
Around the wall, they found two stiff bands and two stretchy ones.
Near the end, the poo dries out, and that uneven squeeze presses in the corners!
So the cubes are shaped inside the wombat, not on the way out.
The lead scientist, Patricia Yang, even tested whether they roll like dice!
In 2019, the team won an Ig Nobel Prize for physics!
Now Yang hopes factories can learn a new way to make cubes.
Until then, the best cube machine on Earth is still a wombat!
